step1_figure.circuit_type: Cascaded inverters with asymmetric capacitive loading
step1_figure.description: A circuit demonstrating how timing skew is introduced into a high-speed digital signal due to mismatched rise and fall times caused by asymmetric loading (a 100fF capacitor on the first inverter's output).

t_PHL_inv1.description: High-to-low propagation delay of the first inverter.

source.reference: Discussion of Fig 18.13 and Eq 18.7 (adapted for standard inverter)

equation.explanation: The time it takes for the NMOS to discharge the load capacitor to VDD/2.
equation.assumptions: R_eq,n is the equivalent resistance of the NMOS in saturation/triode, roughly (3/4)*(VDD/I_DSATn).

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the dominant 100fF load and the strong NMOS drive current.

t_PLH_inv1.description: Low-to-high propagation delay of the first inverter.

source.reference: Discussion of Fig 18.13 and Eq 18.8 (adapted for standard inverter)

equation.explanation: The time it takes for the PMOS to charge the load capacitor to VDD/2.
equation.assumptions: R_eq,p is the equivalent resistance of the PMOS, roughly (3/4)*(VDD/I_DSATp).

sky130_expected.reasoning: The PMOS is much weaker than the NMOS (lower mobility), leading to a significantly longer rise time for the same 100fF load.

t_delay_rise.description: Total propagation delay from the input going high to the final output (out2) going high.

source.reference: Text discussion of Fig 18.14: 'The total delay is the sum of t_PHL + t_PLH'

equation.explanation: When Vin goes high, inv1 output goes low (t_PHL1), causing inv2 output to go high (t_PLH2).
equation.assumptions: t_PLH2 is very small because the second inverter has minimal capacitive loading.

sky130_expected.calculation:
1. t_PHL1 ≈ 36.2 ps.
2. Assuming inv2 load is ~5fF (intrinsic), t_PLH2 ≈ 0.69 * 2836 * 5fF ≈ 9.8 ps.
3. t_delay_rise = 36.2ps + 9.8ps = 46 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the fast high-to-low transition of the first inverter.

t_delay_fall.description: Total propagation delay from the input going low to the final output (out2) going low.

source.reference: Text discussion of Fig 18.14: 'resulting in the same sum (t_PHL + t_PLH)'

equation.explanation: When Vin goes low, inv1 output goes high (t_PLH1), causing inv2 output to go low (t_PHL2).
equation.assumptions: t_PHL2 is very small because the second inverter has minimal capacitive loading.

sky130_expected.calculation:
1. t_PLH1 ≈ 195.7 ps.
2. Assuming inv2 load is ~5fF (intrinsic), t_PHL2 ≈ 0.69 * 525 * 5fF ≈ 1.8 ps.
3. t_delay_fall = 195.7ps + 1.8ps = 197.5 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the slow low-to-high transition of the first inverter due to the weak PMOS driving 100fF.

skew.description: The time skew added to the input signal, calculated as the difference between the total rise delay and total fall delay.

source.reference: Text discussion of Fig 18.13: 'the time skew added to the input signal can add up and result in timing errors'

equation.explanation: Measures the asymmetry in propagation delays which alters the pulse width of the transmitted signal.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The large difference is directly caused by the mobility difference between NMOS and PMOS when driving a heavy asymmetric load.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure propagation delays and skew of the cascaded inverters with asymmetric loading.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Fig 18.13 Skew Circuit
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Define parameters for W/L=10
.param W_xm1=1.5 L_xm1=0.15
.param W_xm2=1.5 L_xm2=0.15
.param W_xm3=1.5 L_xm3=0.15
.param W_xm4=1.5 L_xm4=0.15

* DUT
xm1 Vout Vin 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm2 Vout Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
C1 Vout 0 1e-13
xm3 Vout2 Vout 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 Vout2 Vout VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}

* Stimulus
Vin Vin 0 PULSE(0 1.8 1n 50p 50p 2n 5n)

.control
tran 10p 5n

* Measure t_PHL_inv1 (Vin rising, Vout falling)
meas tran t_PHL_inv1 trig v(Vin) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 fall=1

* Measure t_PLH_inv1 (Vin falling, Vout rising)
meas tran t_PLH_inv1 trig v(Vin) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure t_delay_rise (Vin rising, Vout2 rising)
meas tran t_delay_rise trig v(Vin) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Vout2) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure t_delay_fall (Vin falling, Vout2 falling)
meas tran t_delay_fall trig v(Vin) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(Vout2) val=0.9 fall=1

* Calculate skew
let skew = abs(t_delay_rise - t_delay_fall)
print skew

quit
.endc
.end
